methodology.wall_clock: perf/run.php, 5 warm repeats, uncached policy. See after-cache.json and baseline.json.
methodology.xdebug: php -d xdebug.mode=profile per scenario (AARO_PERF_REPEATS=1). Summarized with perf/summarize_cachegrind.php. Profiler adds large overhead; use wall clock for seconds, Xdebug for ranking.
methodology.note: Function-block sums in cachegrind are useful for ranking, not for adding to 100% across nested calls.

scaling.columns: 200 rows at 2 columns ~0.08s vs 16 columns ~6.5s (~80x). Cost scales with schema width, not row count alone.
scaling.repository_layer: getCurrent ~2x entity path (~13s vs ~6.5s) for same 200 rows.
scaling.schema_cache: after-cache uncached vs baseline main uncached: wide read unchanged (~6.5s). Caching removes DESCRIBE; it does not remove per-row enrichment.

holistic_conclusion: The database is not the bottleneck for list reads and repository hydration on MariaDB.
Every row pays a full-schema walk on next(): FieldOperation build + hasField (with fuzzy match even on success).
Repository getCurrent adds fieldTypeConversions and property/entity assignment, which shows up as PerfOrderEntity __get/__set and dominates that scenario.
Schema/metadata caching is still worth keeping for clear/fetch/id loops and multi-worker deployments, but it will not fix wide reads.
Next wins align with latency milestones L-03 through L-06: lazy hasField, read-only row bind, reuse field map, trim type conversion.
